candidate_law.name: absorption-limited authorized-strength capability ceiling
candidate_law.setup: A military formation begins at personnel target T with experience E, loses fraction ell, and can receive replacements of experience E_R<E. The target T and all other capability factors remain fixed. A cohort N=n*T enters an empty training pipeline; there is initially no trained reserve; all available trained replacements can be assigned to this formation until its personnel target is refilled.
candidate_law.authorized_strength_ceiling: If the pipeline is sufficient to refill the target, lim C_m/C_0 at r_m=ell equals 1-ell*(1-q)<1 whenever E_R<E.
candidate_law.headcount_refill_condition: Finite eventual refill from the one-time cohort requires n*b>ell. The first interval index reaching target is ceil(log(1-ell/(n*b))/log(a)) when 0<a<1.

predictions: Production deploy_military never deploys more than the personnel deficit to target, even when offered arbitrarily large replacement mass.
Once the target is refilled, another deploy_military call returns zero if no new deficit appears.
For E_R<E, capability recovery is monotone in absorbed replacement r_m but its fixed-target ceiling remains below 1.
More training throughput shortens time to nominal headcount recovery but does not change the veterancy-limited capability ceiling.
A one-time recruit cohort equal exactly to personnel losses cannot achieve finite-time full headcount refill when reserve attrition is positive; extra intake is required.
production_equivalence_required: A real initialized military formation at target must accept exactly its induced deficit and no more from deploy_military.
The production experience after full target refill must equal the SL7 weighted replacement value using E_R=0.10.
A second oversized deployment attempt with no new deficit must deploy exactly zero.
The analytic r_m trajectory must match an explicit recurrence of SL10 graduation, reserve attrition, and target-capped deployment across the stress grid.
claim_boundary: SL11 is a theorem of Pineland's synthetic training, target-strength, replacement-memory, and combat-capability equations. It does not prescribe real force-structure or replacement policy.
